answer:
HYPOTHESIS (natural language, data-grounded):

Within the NLSY79 1989 cross-section (ages 24–32), age has essentially no influence on the likelihood of withdrawing more money from savings than putting in (DISSAVED=1). After removing an artifact — 2,151 exact duplicate rows generated by mean-imputed INCOME and BMI records — the probability of dissaving is stable at roughly 26–30% across every single year of age (24: 27.2%; 27: 28.8%; 29: 30.2%; 31: 29.4%; 32: 27.9%), and in the primary logistic model (dedup, n = 10,535; controls log(1+INCOME), gender, race, BMI winsorized at the 1st/99th percentile) the per-year age odds ratio is 1.007 (95% CI 0.988–1.026, p = 0.48). Adding AGE_2 does not improve fit (LRT χ²(1) = 0.64, p = 0.42), so there is no evidence of curvature. Excluding the 103 distinct rows with both INCOME and BMI at the imputed mean constant leaves results essentially unchanged (OR 1.006, p = 0.52), and a three-category multinomial check (dissave vs. save vs. no-change/no-savings) agrees (dissave-vs-save age OR 0.995, p = 0.69). What the data does support: dissaving behavior in this cohort is strongly stratified by income (higher log-income → more likely to dissave; OR ≈ e^0.25 ≈ 1.29 per log unit) and modestly by gender and race (women and Black respondents ~13–18% higher odds), but not by age within this narrow window. What it does not support: any claim about life-cycle aging, causality, or behavior outside ages 24–32 — "age" here is cohort position in a single 1989 snapshot.

DIVERGENCE FLAG (raw vs. dedup — the most defensible reading): On the raw file, age appears strongly protective (OR 0.954 per year, p = 4×10⁻⁷; rates falling 25.5% at 24 → 18.2% at 32, with a nominally significant quadratic term). We diagnose this as artifact-contaminated, not real: 3,963 rows carry INCOME exactly equal to the column mean (47.27906…) and 2,493 carry BMI exactly equal to the column mean (25.15894…) — signatures of mean imputation (a mean-imputed column keeps its mean exactly). The 2,200 rows imputed on BOTH variables produce 2,097 of the 2,151 duplicates, have a DISSAVED rate of only ~1%, and are concentrated at ages 29–32; this manufactured the spurious negative gradient. Critically, this imputation diagnosis is an inference from exact-equality with the column means — it is NOT a documented flag in the data, so the raw-file result is reported but not trusted. The deduplicated estimate is the primary reading; we do not average the two stories.

SECONDARY OUTCOME (interpreted cautiously): SAMESAVE ("no change OR no savings" — an economically conflated category) shows a marginally negative, near-null age association in the primary model (OR 0.984 per year, p = 0.066); given the conflation, we do not interpret this as evidence of an age effect.

Limitations: single cross-section (no causal/life-cycle claims); age range only 24–32, so curvature is weakly identified; imputation inferred, not documented; INCOME units inferred as thousands of 1989 dollars; SAMESAVE conflates two behaviors; BMI extremes (max 176.4) handled by winsorization, with results insensitive to it.

Workflow summary: (1) loaded data/nls_bmi_processed.csv (12,686 × 9, zero missingness); (2) diagnosed duplication/imputation (exact duplicates = 2,151; mean-imputed constants identified); (3) built three analysis samples — raw (12,686, labeled artifact-contaminated), deduplicated primary (10,535), dedup + excluding both-mean-imputed rows (10,432); (4) for each: single-year-age DISSAVED rates with 95% Wilson CIs, logistic regressions DISSAVED ~ AGE (+ AGE_2) + log(1+INCOME) + FEMALE + BLACK + HISPANIC + BMI_winsorized, LRT for linear-vs-quadratic age, secondary logit on SAMESAVE, and MNLogit three-category robustness; (5) reported all three stories side by side with the divergence flagged. Executed script: analysis/run_analysis.py; full output: analysis/results.txt.

payload.hypothesis: Within the NLSY79 1989 cross-section (ages 24-32), age has essentially no influence on the likelihood of DISSAVED=1. After removing 2,151 exact duplicate rows caused by mean-imputed INCOME/BMI records, the probability of dissaving is stable at roughly 26-30% at every single year of age, with a per-year age odds ratio of 1.007 (95% CI 0.988-1.026, p=0.48) in the primary logistic model, and no evidence of curvature (AGE_2 LRT p=0.42). The apparent protective age effect in the raw file (OR 0.954/yr, p=4e-7) is diagnosed as an artifact of mean-imputed rows (DISSAVED rate ~1%, concentrated at ages 29-32) that duplicated 2,097 times; this diagnosis is inferred from exact equality with column means, not a documented flag. Dissaving is instead stratified by income (OR ~1.29 per log unit), gender (women higher), and race (Black respondents higher).
payload.workflow: Inspection -> imputation/duplication diagnosis -> three analysis samples (raw 12,686 labeled artifact-contaminated; dedup primary 10,535; dedup+excl both-imputed 10,432) -> per-sample single-year-age rates with Wilson CIs -> logistic DISSAVED ~ AGE (+AGE_2) + log(1+INCOME) + GENDER + BLACK + HISPANIC + BMI winsorized(1/99), LRT for curvature -> secondary logit on SAMESAVE -> three-category multinomial robustness -> divergence flagged, no averaging.
